character_facts: Aghnar is a child whose mother has died.
Honorata is the mother of Aghnar and is the deceased figure being shown or remembered.
The father is physically unwell or strained in this scene, as indicated by coughing in his speech.
The father is actively indoctrinating the children with the memory of Honorata's death.
At least one child is emotionally distressed and objects that the situation is unfair.
characters_present: Honorata (as projected image, memory, or visual representation)
An adult male identified in dialogue as 'Father'
At least one additional child near the father
continuity_links: This page establishes or reinforces a blood-feud motive against the Shabda-Oud.
The scene ties family memory, parental command, and revenge into the upbringing of Aghnar and the other child.
dialogue_meaning: Aghnar is being forced to witness his mother's death as a formative memory.
One child protests the cruelty or unfairness of what is happening.
The father announces Honorata's death and links it to an obligation of vengeance.
The Shabda-Oud are named as the future target of that revenge.
A child accepts the father's command and repeats the vow.
locations: A circular industrial or ceremonial platform
A desert or barren landscape with a distant tower-like structure
An interior observation area or compartment overlooking the energy sphere
lore_facts: Honorata is dead by the end of this scene.
The father's side holds the Shabda-Oud responsible enough to target them for annihilation.
Honorata's death is associated with an 'explosion of her heart' in the dialogue.
The family treats this death as a defining memory and a basis for inherited revenge.
plot_events: A giant image or recording of a woman identified as Honorata is displayed or remembered on a massive scale.
A child named Aghnar is ordered to keep watching his mother's end so he will never forget it.
A bright spherical energy event is shown as the apparent moment or symbol of Honorata's death.
An adult male, apparently the father, declares that Honorata is gone and frames her death as something to be avenged.
The father specifically vows future destruction of the Shabda-Oud.
A child agrees to avenge the mother.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the giant female image is a live projection, a recorded memorial, or a stylized visual metaphor.
The exact identity of the additional child or children at the bottom of the page is not explicit from this page alone.
Some dialogue is small and partially difficult to read, so exact wording may be slightly uncertain.
The precise mechanism of Honorata's death is not visually explained beyond the glowing sphere and the father's reference to her heart exploding.
visual_summary: A two-page spread centers on a monumental, translucent image of a woman’s head projected above a circular industrial platform in a reddish desert setting. On the facing page, intense beams and a glowing sphere suggest a violent energy event or memorialized detonation. Along the bottom, a dark-haired adult and children watch or recall the scene from an interior vantage point, with one child distressed and the adult turning the mother’s death into a vow of future revenge.
